items.title: Father Al Lewis Interview, 1972-02-21
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Has Uncle Jim's on Carrollton? Yeah. James LaRocca. [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah, I wonder if he's still living, he might be, yeah, he might be.

ctx.x: That was right after, let me see, that was around 40, I remember we had another group before that, but I'll get back to that. We was working at Buckaroo with this man, Charlie Hamilton was playing piano, and Old Man James was playing alto sax, and Brady was playing drums.
Old Man James that played bass, he was playing alto? Yeah, playing alto.

His brother played alto. Squeak's daddy, his brother died, went to California and died, his brother played alto. We used to work for St. Charles, Louis James' brother. And then we left- You had Brady on? Well Brady was drums. Which Brady? Brady the drum player, I don't know, you sure? Brady Smith, yeah. Yeah, Brady Smith was playing drums, Charlie Hamilton was playing piano. Charlie Hamilton got that car when he drives his day, he made that offer tipsy board off of that job with Buckaroo, St. Charles. St. James.…
